note: Contract 2.32 (#817), building on the Host yield policy #816 gave the Python Runner. Two different things are pinned here and they must not be collapsed: the policy a host resolves, and the state the Run discloses. On macOS the policy is the utility QoS clamp, and nice and the background clamp do not qualify as one -- #788's measurements put foreground throughput at 2.62 of 12 cores under nice -n 10 against 10.52 under the utility clamp, and the background clamp starves the Run itself. A platform with no declared policy resolves its Config to none, because there is nothing to apply, but discloses unsupported: none is an operator's opt-out, and a host that was never offered the choice has not opted out of anything. A consumer reads an absent disclosure on an old trace as unknown, never as an inferred value.
